response.markdown_report:
Select a **candidate-conditioned recent-history residual** for the next experiment. At 10% progress, a small scoring change offers a clearer test than another temporal architecture.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Zero initialization preserves baseline scores initially. This makes an added branch easier to evaluate safely. (2) Recent pooling compresses several actions into one vector. Candidate-specific weighting could retain distinctions that shared pooling loses. (3) Prior residual variants scored 0.4575 and 0.4138 versus the supplied baseline’s 0.5050. These observations discourage repeating increasingly complex pooling, although they do not isolate why performance declined.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Multi-Level Interaction Reranking [1] motivates candidate–history interactions. Such interactions can test whether a candidate has specific historical support. (2) MiaSRec [2] challenges last-item dominance through multiple session representations. This favors retaining several recent items rather than replacing SASRec with last-item similarity. (3) gSASRec [3] motivates objective-only experiments with more negatives. Its calibration findings do not establish that a new scoring branch improves HR@10.

**Framework and directions.** Separate three axes: evidence selection, scoring, and optimization. Fixed recent pooling selects evidence before seeing the candidate; candidate attention selects evidence during scoring; multiple-negative objectives change competition without changing evidence. The next gap to test is candidate-specific evidence, with optimization held fixed.

**Ideas and assessments.** Scores are originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Scores | Assessment: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate-conditioned recent residual [1,2] | 4/7/7/6/4 | O: targeted combination / established attention; F: extensible / incremental; U: specific support / similarity can mislead; M: candidate separation / no proven margin benefit; D: small scorer / predictor integration |
| Scratch TF-IDF recent-content residual | 4/6/7/5/5 | O: permitted content fusion / familiar matching; F: interpretable / lexical sparsity; U: finer distinctions / wording misses intent; M: extra evidence / margins may worsen; D: lightweight features / vocabulary and mapping work |
| Uniform 32-negative objective only [3] | 2/6/4/8/3 | O: controlled test / established; F: reusable / limited novelty; U: stronger competition / no purpose signal; M: targets wrong ranks / false negatives; D: simple loss / sampling cost |

**Chosen mechanism.** Keep SASRec intact. Add a zero-scaled score residual using candidate attention over the latest five causal input embeddings, conditioned additionally on the SASRec state. This explicitly targets unsupported broad associations and missed entertainment mood/intensity distinctions; neither compatibility nor ownership is inferred.

The model-facing target is the observed 17.4–24.0% training wrong-rank rate, especially Industrial_and_Scientific. These are training diagnostics, not validation results. Compare baseline versus residual with unchanged loss, then consider objective changes separately. Select exclusively through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Add a candidate-conditioned recent-history scoring residual to the unchanged category-specific SASRec backbone. For each candidate, attend over up to five causal input-item embeddings using both the candidate embedding and the existing SASRec state. Add the resulting candidate-specific score through a learned scalar initialized exactly to zero. Evaluate this architecture change with the baseline loss and negative sampler before testing any objective changes.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies unsupported broad associations and entertainment recommendations that miss specific mood or intensity distinctions. Candidate-conditioned matching tests whether each proposed item has support in particular recent actions, instead of relying exclusively on one shared pooled representation. This is a hypothesis about specificity, not evidence of compatibility, ownership, satisfied demand, or actual user intent. Quantitatively, sampled negatives beat positives in 17.4–24.0% of training pairs, with Industrial_and_Scientific weakest. The scoring residual provides a targeted opportunity to improve candidate separation while retaining the stronger baseline sequence model. Last-item dot products perform poorly in the supplied training probes, so this branch supplements SASRec and retains several recent actions.
idea.implementation_notes:
For valid position t and candidate i, let h be the unchanged SASRec feature and e_i the shared candidate embedding. Collect raw shared input embeddings e_j from nonpadding positions max(0,t-4)..t. Define q = W_h LayerNorm(h) + W_i LayerNorm(e_i), k_j = W_k LayerNorm(e_j), and attention logits q·k_j/sqrt(D) - (t-j). Use bias-free projections initialized normally, and softmax only over valid causal inputs. Compute m = sum_j attention_j * e_j and branch score b = dot(LayerNorm(e_i), LayerNorm(W_v m))/sqrt(D). Return dot(h,e_i) + tanh(a)*b, with a initialized to zero. Empty windows produce exactly zero branch scores. Padding targets are excluded from loss. Do not normalize or otherwise modify the original SASRec score. Initialize new modules with an independent RNG and copy matching backbone tensors from the canonical baseline initialization; a common seed alone does not guarantee matching weights.

Keep baseline BCE, optimizer, data ordering, batch size, and training negative sampler unchanged for the first comparison. This isolates the scoring change; multiple-negative training is a separate future trial. Candidate attention costs O(B*K*5*D) at a prediction position. Chunk full-catalog candidates so the twenty simulator users still receive exact unseen-item rankings without allocating a user-by-catalog-by-history tensor. Chunking must preserve scores and ranking. Do not add a catalog prefilter.

Because candidate dependence no longer fits into a single candidate-independent fused feature, keep log2feats(sequence) returning SASRec features and add a shared score_candidates(features, items, recent_context) method. Have the diagnostic view cache context for its immediately preceding log2feats call; predict_score must use that aligned context and the same scoring method as inference. Reject stale or mismatched cached shapes. Use an explicit context argument internally wherever possible. Preserve supported B x L and B x L x K item layouts, and the public loader tuple (None, sequence, positive, negative). view.model remains the actual trained module and view.item_emb remains the shared embedding. Adapt every probe to the total candidate-conditioned score, including full-catalog recommendations and training margins. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and definitions. Keep unsupported positional interventions marked unsupported. Restore model mode and RNG states after diagnosis.

Save all projection, normalization, scalar, window, and baseline configuration values beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs this exact scorer with all four dataset routes. Verify zero-gate baseline parity, checkpoint reload parity, candidate-chunk parity, padding handling, and causal-prefix invariance before training. Do not claim zero-gate equality of subsequent training trajectories because the new branch consumes computations and eventually learns.

Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, the original splits, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Use no unavailable metadata, reviews, pretrained weights, extra datasets, or hidden test files. Predeclare the baseline/residual comparison, equal checkpoint opportunities, and earliest-checkpoint tie breaking. Select only with the host's unchanged macro validation HR@10 protocol: 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42. Report category results and the number of validation comparisons; do not replace host validation with diagnostic training HR@10. Track all training, diagnostic, debugging, and failed-trial GPU time against the shared 43,200-second budget. The supplied prior scores are observations from earlier variants, not a controlled causal comparison. No execution or new measured results are reported here.
idea.pseudocode:
class CandidateRecentResidual(SASRec):
    initialize baseline backbone unchanged
    initialize independent bias-free projections and branch LayerNorms
    a = Parameter(0.0)

    def encode(sequence):
        h = baseline_log2feats(sequence)
        context = causal_windows(item_emb(sequence), valid=sequence != 0, width=5)
        return h, context

    def score_candidates(h, candidates, context):
        e = item_emb(candidates)
        q = W_h(LN_h(h)) + W_i(LN_i(e))
        k = W_k(LN_k(context.embeddings))
        logits = dot(q, k) / sqrt(D) - context.position_gaps
        weights = masked_softmax_with_zero_empty_rows(logits, context.valid)
        m = weighted_sum(weights, context.embeddings)
        branch = dot(LN_i(e), LN_v(W_v(m))) / sqrt(D)
        branch = zero_for_empty_context(branch)
        return dot(h, e) + tanh(a) * branch

for category in four_required_categories:
    load unchanged baseline split using preprocessing seed 0
    copy canonical seed-42 backbone initialization
    for batch in baseline_training_loader:
        _, sequence, positive, negative = batch
        h, context = model.encode(sequence)
        positive_score = model.score_candidates(h, positive, context)
        negative_score = model.score_candidates(h, negative, context)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_BCE(positive_score, negative_score, valid_targets)
        take_baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
    save exact category model, mappings, and configuration below trial directory

regenerate working/predict.py through the predictor writer
use the same score_candidates implementation in inference and diagnostic adapters
score full catalogs in exact candidate chunks for required simulator users
compare registered baseline and residual trials with unchanged host macro validation HR@10
record every validation opportunity and all charged GPU time

originality.positive: Candidate-conditioned evidence selection offers a distinct, testable alternative to the prior candidate-independent recent pooling branches.
originality.negative: Candidate–history attention and zero-initialized residuals are established techniques; this is an incremental combination.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled test would support subsequent permitted content matching or temporal evidence selection without replacing SASRec.
future_potential.negative: Collaborative similarity may still reinforce broad associations, and fixed sampled validation improvements may not transfer to full-catalog usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The branch uses existing embeddings and a five-item window, requiring no additional data pipeline.
code_difficulty.negative: Candidate-dependent scores require careful diagnostic adaptation, exact full-catalog chunking, and synchronized predictor reconstruction.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequence encoder and shared item-dot-product scoring baseline retained by this proposal.
limitations: Its shared sequence representation does not itself implement the proposed candidate-specific recent-history attention.

related_work.title: Multi-Level Interaction Reranking
contributions: Provides precedent for candidate–history interactions and personalized long- and short-term attention, motivating idea 1.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this minimal residual under the supplied four-category RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: MiaSRec
contributions: Uses item-centered session representations and dynamic intent selection, motivating retention of several recent actions.
limitations: Its session modeling results do not show that the proposed five-item candidate-conditioned branch improves Amazon macro HR@10.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Combines increased negative counts with generalized BCE to address sampling-induced overconfidence, motivating a separate objective direction.
limitations: Does not identify false negatives or validate the proposed candidate-conditioned architecture.
